arguments.decision: Where should a built backfire plugin (deno task backfire:build today) get its own lock file once packages/backfire/uv.lock is replaced by the root workspace uv.lock?
arguments.evidence: packages/backfire/src/backfire_tools/build.py:107 copies pyproject.toml, .python-version and uv.lock from packages/backfire into the built copy. The copy is installed with 'uv sync --frozen --no-dev' (docs/backfire.md:31, with --extra education for the work build) and started with 'uv --directory ${PLUGIN_ROOT}/backfire run --frozen --offline --no-sync backfire serve-mcp' (docs/backfire.md:41, plugins/code/mcp.json, plugins/work/mcp.json). specs/008-doc-consistency/research.md:127-131 records why per-package locks exist: each built plugin is self-contained. The root uv.lock also contains doc-regions and wiki-consistency, so copying it does not give a standalone project lock. Probes on 2026-09-29: 'uv export --package backfire --frozen --no-dev --extra education --format pylock.toml --no-emit-workspace' writes a 38-package pylock.toml; installing from it needs 'uv venv' plus 'uv pip sync pylock.toml' plus installing the project, which changes the documented install command. Writing the exported pins (uv export ... --no-hashes) as [tool.uv] constraint-dependencies into the copy and running 'uv lock --offline' there produced a standalone uv.lock with exactly the same 45 package versions as today's packages/backfire/uv.lock, so the documented install and start commands stay the same.

candidates.description: build.py exports backfire's pinned versions from the root lock and runs 'uv lock --offline' in the built copy with those pins as constraints, so the copy has its own uv.lock and keeps the documented install and start commands.
build.py writes 'uv export --format pylock.toml' into the copy, and the documented install changes to 'uv venv', 'uv pip sync pylock.toml' and a project install.
Keep a separately maintained packages/backfire/uv.lock next to the root uv.lock and copy it as today.

requirements: Keeps the built plugin's documented install and start commands unchanged.
Keeps one source of pinned versions in the repository.
arguments.priorities:
User and repository priorities (verbose-broccoli, feature/turborepo, Linear CHE-32, a trial whose result is a report; nothing is merged):
1. The user chose to move the TypeScript side from Deno to Node.js and to run the three Python packages (backfire, doc-regions, wiki-consistency) as one native uv workspace under Turborepo's experimental Python support.
2. Change only the parts that must change; leave everything else as it is. The smallest change that reaches the goal wins.
3. AGENTS.md reuse order: first existing repository, runtime, standard-library or dependency functionality; then a stable upstream dependency; then an unstable upstream with the smallest patch; last, minimal glue. Minimize locally owned code; prefer reducing locally owned implementation over reducing dependency count. If the goal needs substantial new local implementation, stop and report instead.
4. Requirements that stay: built backfire plugins install offline, stay self-contained and write only into their own .venv; readiness proves the server runs from its own .venv.
5. Dropping a check, changing scope, changing governance documents, or changing the user's global tools (Node, npm, uv, Codex) is the user's decision, not the agent's.
